gold_source: reference/experiment-h-full-vs-minimal-vs-nl.md, Round 2 (S4) — same competition pattern reused verbatim from experiment-g Trial 3, independently reproduced.
prompt:
You will read a short workplace conversation between two colleagues, then answer one question about the final message. Do not explain your uncertainty away — if more than one file genuinely fits, say so.

Turn 1 — Colleague: "Can you get report-final.pdf ready to send to Alex?"
Turn 2 — You: "Sure."
Turn 3 — Colleague: "Also, take a look at report-final-v2.pdf."
Turn 4 — You: "OK."
Turn 5 — Colleague: "And report-final-reviewed.pdf needs attention too."
Turn 6 — You: "Noted."
Turn 7 — Colleague: "Go ahead and send it to Alex."

Question: which file (by exact filename) does Turn 7 instruct you to send, and to whom? If you genuinely cannot tell, say so explicitly instead of guessing.

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"entity": "<filename or 'cannot_determine'>", "recipient": "<name or 'cannot_determine'>", "confidence": "<low|medium|high>"}

metadata.description: Recency (report-final-reviewed.pdf, the most recently mentioned file) competes against verb-semantic binding (report-final.pdf is the only file actually tied to the verb 'send', in Turn 1).
metadata.expected_failure_mode: NL receivers tend to pick the most recently mentioned file (report-final-reviewed.pdf) or report multiple candidates / inability to determine, per experiment-h and experiment-g.
